clue.text: Brew tea: it hastens doctor

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew ingredients together, so the letters that follow get stirred into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these three words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a cuppa, on the grounds that tea speeds up the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a verb meaning tamper with, a classic anagram signal, but here it is the definition and 'Brew' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetist is a medical specialist, a physician who administers anaesthetics, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Feather-brain to help nesting bird

indicators.note: a bird nesting somewhere is settled inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: aid is a synonym of help
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Some scatterbrain is trying to help a bird build its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits inside the word for help: A + RHEA + ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a silly, empty-headed person; 'feather-brain' suggests a head as light as feathers.

clue.text: Pies do for training with a fatty

indicators.note: something put in for training is being drilled and reshaped, so the letters get reorganised

parts.note: the letters as written
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: Pies will fuel the athletic training of an overweight person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fatty' reads as a noun for a person, but the definition is the adjective meaning containing fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the biological adjective for fat tissue, so it means fatty in the sense of consisting of fat.

clue.text: Small (tiny) empty little belly to consume sugary item

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wee is a Scottish and informal word for tiny

indicators.note: an empty container has lost its insides, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: tum is a childish, little word for the belly; only its first and last letters are kept
to eat is to consume food

explanation.surface: A small, tiny tummy wants to consume something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket around 'tiny' is surface decoration only; tum is a British nursery word for stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is an old-fashioned term for a confection such as a candy or sugared fruit, a sugary item.

clue.text: Composer hiding diamonds and gold in lift looks after things temporarily

indicators.note: something hiding another thing conceals it inside itself, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
D is the card-game abbreviation for the diamonds suit

indicators.note: one item placed in another is put inside it

parts.note: to heft is to lift something heavy
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A composer has stashed his jewels and gold in an elevator while someone minds his affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: HOL(D)ST then HEF(OR)T, read across the two grid entries as HOLDS THE FORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold the fort is an idiom meaning to take charge and keep things running while the person responsible is away.

clue.text: Skittish hot pony generates violent storm

indicators.note: a skittish animal is jumpy and restless, so the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A nervous, overheated pony kicks up a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, a particularly violent storm with very strong winds.

clue.text: Tip monarch to succeed son as keeper of order in house

indicators.note: to succeed something is to come after it, so these pieces are placed behind the other

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a peak is the tip or top of something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Advice that the king should take over from his son and keep the household in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip monarch to succeed son' sounds like a betting tip on royal succession; 'house' is the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker presides over the House of Commons and keeps order during debates, calling 'Order!'.

clue.text: Sweet-talks to bed in Brontë's first chapter

indicators.note: placed in the following letters means put between them, sitting inside
the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the novelist's surname
to utter is to speak
a cot is a small bed
CH is the standard abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talks their way into bed in the opening chapter of a Brontë novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen tempts you to read 'Sweet-talks' as one word; split it and 'Sweet' is the definition, with the talking and the bed sitting between two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection made from butter and brown sugar, a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Republic's informal music maker taking shower

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: uke is the casual short form of ukulele, a small guitar-like instrument
a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: A country's casual musician goes off to have a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: UK(RAIN)E: 'shower' suggests bathing, but it is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is an independent Eastern European state with an elected president, a republic since 1991.

clue.text: Do this if unable to hear one present in principal role

definitions.text: Do this if unable to hear

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: the lead is the main part in a play or film
the Roman numeral for one
pr. is the grammatical abbreviation for present tense

explanation.surface: Advice that a deaf actor in the lead role should follow the other speakers' mouths.
explanation.walkthrough: I + PR sit inside LEAD after its first letter. PR for present is a dictionary abbreviation rarely seen outside grammar books.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by watching the speaker's mouth, a skill used by people with hearing loss.

clue.text: Sites cleaned in preparation for food outlet

indicators.note: ingredients in preparation are being chopped and arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Premises are scrubbed ready for opening a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods such as cooked meats and cheeses, so a retail outlet for food.

clue.text: See 4
Inhaling potassium, loners damaged breathing apparatus

indicators.note: something inhaling takes material in, so one piece ends up inside another
damaged things are broken up and out of shape, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters as written
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Isolated people harmed by breathing in a chemical need breathing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a tube that lets a swimmer breathe air while face down in the water, a simple breathing device.

clue.text: Beg direction about securing top of roof

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters run the other way
securing means holding fast inside, so the letters are held within the words before

parts.note: found across the two words, starting inside the first

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for directions about how to fix the top of a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EGDIR span 'Beg direction' and read backwards give RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge is the horizontal line at the apex of a pitched roof where the two slopes meet.

clue.text: Unusual English coin's first money given to most of wealthy

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the final letter is dropped
one piece given to another is attached to it, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of coin
a cent is a small unit of money
rich is a synonym of wealthy

explanation.surface: An odd English coin is the first money handed over to the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unconventional in behaviour, deviating from what is usual.

clue.text: With which to disguise Tory (Anglican) having drink with Russian premier?

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church
ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: the premier item is the one that comes first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A churchgoing Conservative politician hides behind drinks with the Russian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a politician to join the Tory, but it only picks a first letter. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealer is a cosmetic used to mask blemishes, so it is what you would use to disguise them.

clue.text: Pointless heir to the throne with possible evidence of having been on holiday's a fraud

indicators.note: pointless here means stripped of compass points, so any north, south, east or west letters go

parts.note: Charles was long the heir to the British throne

parts.words: possible evidence of having been on holiday
parts.note: a suntan is what a holiday abroad may leave on the skin

explanation.surface: A useless prince with a holiday suntan turns out to be an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the compass points E and S from the end of the prince's name leaves CHARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is someone who falsely claims special knowledge or skill, a fraud or quack.

clue.text: Supplier of gas to upwardly mobile degenerate locality

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means reading from bottom to top, the opposite direction

parts.note: to rot is to decay or degenerate
an area is a locality or district

explanation.surface: Gas is supplied to a run-down neighbourhood full of social climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly mobile' suggests social climbing, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerator is a device that forces air into soil or liquid, so something that supplies gas.

clue.text: Abhorred mass retaining essence of pantheism

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a load is a mass or great quantity

indicators.note: the essence is the heart of a thing, so only the central letters are taken

parts.note: the three central letters of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: Many people detested a core belief that god is everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to feel intense hatred or disgust, so loathed matches abhorred as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Assume mine contains bone

indicators.note: something that contains another holds it within

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that a mine has fossil bones in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as true, to assume or postulate it as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Treat at the cinema when blue movie features bent cop?

indicators.note: a film that features something has it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a blue movie is pornography

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A cinema snack bought while watching an adult film starring a crooked policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' is British slang for corrupt, which suits the surface, but here it twists the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is the classic snack bought and eaten while watching films in a movie theatre.

clue.text: Educated in fashionable language

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: swish is informal for smart or stylish
ed. is the abbreviation for educated, as in biographical notes

explanation.surface: A cultured person schooled in the language of the smart set.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedish is the North Germanic tongue spoken in Sweden and parts of Finland.

clue.text: "Twister" divided a party

parts.note: torn means split or divided
taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: The film Twister split a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the film title, but they just mark the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an informal American name for a tornado, a violently rotating column of air.

clue.text: Group initially only contained two elderly tenors

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A choir started out with just two old tenors.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight, especially eight musicians performing together, so a group.

clue.text: Reps having sex broke fast

indicators.note: something that broke has fallen to pieces, so its letters are put back in another order

parts.note: the letters as written
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Sales representatives having an affair broke their vows of abstinence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke fast' looks like a phrase about ending a fast; 'broke' is the anagram signal and 'fast' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Express means fast or high-speed, as in an express train or express delivery.

clue.text: Hospital occupational therapist to discharge important person

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
OT is the usual abbreviation for occupational therapist
a shot is the discharge of a gun

explanation.surface: A hospital therapist is told to send home a VIP patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' suggests releasing a patient, which fits the hospital, but it means a firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is an informal term for a very successful or important person, a big shot.

clue.text: A long time in queue's beastly

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: a line is a queue
an eon is an immeasurably long period

explanation.surface: Waiting ages in a queue is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' reads as horrible, but here it means like a beast; the lion is the beast meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means resembling or relating to a lion, so it is literally like a wild animal.

clue.text: Financial crisis clubs direct badly? Hasten to church!

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for the clubs suit

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters as written
to run is to hurry
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: In a money crisis, the advice is to rush to church and pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit crunch is a sudden sharp reduction in lending by banks, as in the 2008 crash, a kind of financial crisis.
